analysis: The item-bias experiment achieved host-validated macro HR@10 of 0.5125, improving by 0.0025 over the previous 0.510 and by 0.0075 over baseline 0.505. Category HR@10 was Movies_and_TV 0.515, Industrial_and_Scientific 0.540, Electronics 0.425, and CDs_and_Vinyl 0.570. This is a modest observed improvement consistent with the item-intercept hypothesis, but it does not establish the cause or statistical reliability. Electronics remains the weakest category; prior per-category scores were not supplied, so category-level improvements cannot be inferred. The proposed 0.520–0.530 range was not reached. Allocated GPU time was 1178.55 seconds.
code_summary: Each category trains one SASRec with 64-dimensional tied item embeddings, learned positions, two causal attention blocks, one attention head, dropout 0.5, and a jointly trained scalar item bias initialized to zero without consuming random numbers. Scores are sequence–item dot products plus item bias. Training preserves dense causal supervision, 32 uniform negatives excluding training-history items, unsmoothed sampled softmax, per-user loss normalization, 512-position checkpointed scoring chunks, and AdamW. Bias weights are explicit checkpoint inputs for gradient propagation. Validation selects one checkpoint per category by strict HR@10 improvement with 40-epoch patience. The generated predictor reconstructs the same architecture, strictly loads the complete checkpoint, and routes each dataset to exactly one model. No ensemble or separately fitted scorer is used.
